paragraphs: "Cash Rent Change" means the percentage change in the base rent of the lease commenced during the period compared to the base rent of the Comparable Lease for assets included in the Operating Portfolio. The calculation compares the first base rent payment due after the lease commencement date compared to the base rent of the last monthly payment due prior to the termination of the lease, excluding holdover rent. Rent under gross or similar type leases are converted to a net rent based on an estimate of the applicable recoverable expenses.
"Comparable Lease" means a lease in the same space with a similar lease structure as compared to the previous in-place lease, excluding new leases for space that was not occupied under our ownership.
"GAAP" means generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America.

"New Lease" means a lease that is signed for an initial term equal to or greater than 12 months for any vacant space, including a lease signed by a new tenant or an existing tenant that is expanding into new (additional) space.

"Occupancy rate" means the percentage of total leasable square footage for which either revenue recognition has commenced in accordance with GAAP or the lease term has commenced as of the close of the reporting period, whichever occurs earlier.

"Operating Portfolio" means all buildings that were acquired stabilized or have achieved Stabilization. The Operating Portfolio excludes non-core flex/office buildings, buildings contained in the Value Add Portfolio, and buildings classified as held for sale.

"Renewal Lease" means a lease signed by an existing tenant to extend the term for 12 months or more, including (i) a renewal of the same space as the current lease at lease expiration, (ii) a renewal of only a portion of the current space at lease expiration, or (iii) an early renewal or workout, which ultimately does extend the original term for 12 months or more.

"Straight-line Rent Change" means the percentage change in the average monthly base rent over the term of the lease that commenced during the period compared to the Comparable Lease for assets included in the Operating Portfolio. Rent under gross or similar type leases are converted to a net rent based on an estimate of the applicable recoverable expenses, and this calculation excludes the impact of any holdover rent.

"Stabilization" for properties under development or being redeveloped means the earlier of achieving 90% occupancy or 12 months after completion. With respect to properties acquired and immediately added to the Value Add Portfolio, (i) if acquired with less than 75% occupancy as of the acquisition date, Stabilization will occur upon the earlier of achieving 90% occupancy or 12 months from the acquisition date, or (ii) if acquired and will be less than 75% occupied due to known move-outs within two years of the acquisition date, Stabilization will occur upon the earlier of achieving 90% occupancy after the known move-outs have occurred or 12 months after the known move-outs have occurred.

"Total annualized base rental revenue" means the monthly base cash rent for the applicable property or properties as of December 31, 2025 (which is different from rent calculated in accordance with GAAP for purposes of our financial statements), multiplied by 12. If a tenant is in a free rent period as of December 31, 2025, the annualized rent is calculated based on the first contractual monthly base rent amount multiplied by 12.

"Value Add Portfolio" means our properties that meet any of the following criteria: (i) less than 75% occupied as of the acquisition date; (ii) will be less than 75% occupied due to known move-outs within two years of the acquisition date; (iii) out of service with significant physical renovation of the asset; or (iv) development.

"Weighted Average Lease Term" means the contractual lease term in years, assuming that tenants exercise no renewal options, purchase options, or early termination rights, as of the lease start date weighted by square footage. Weighted Average Lease Term related to acquired assets reflects the remaining lease term in years as of the acquisition date weighted by square footage.

We are a REIT focused on the acquisition, ownership, development, and operation of industrial properties throughout the United States. Our platform is designed to (i) identify properties for acquisition that offer attractive returns across CBRE-EA Tier 1 industrial real estate markets, industries, and tenants, (ii) provide growth through our ownership of high-quality assets, property management and pursuit of acquisitions in an attractive opportunity set, and (iii) capitalize our business appropriately given the characteristics of our assets.

We are organized and conduct our operations to maintain our qualification as a REIT under Sections 856 through 860 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"), and generally are not subject to federal income tax to the extent we currently distribute our income to our stockholders and maintain our qualification as a REIT. We remain subject to state and local taxes on our income and property and to U.S. federal income and excise taxes on our undistributed income.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
Adverse economic conditions may adversely affect our operating results and financial condition.
Inflation, rising interest rates, and developments that affect the financial services industry, may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of other operations.
Trade policies, tariffs and related government actions may cause a decline in economic activity and have a material adverse impact on our business.
Our investments are in the industrial real estate sector, and we would be adversely affected by an economic downturn in that sector.
We are subject to geographic and industry concentrations that make us susceptible to adverse events with respect to certain markets and industries.
We have owned many of our properties for a limited time, and we may not be aware of their characteristics or deficiencies.
Our growth depends, in part, upon acquisitions of properties, and we may be unable to consummate acquisitions on advantageous terms and acquisitions may not perform as we expect.
We may face risks associated with acquiring properties in unfamiliar markets.
A significant portion of our properties have leases that expire in the next two years and we may be unable to renew leases, lease vacant space or re-lease space on favorable terms.
We face significant competition for tenants, which may negatively impact the occupancy and rental rates at our properties.
Default by one or more of our tenants could materially and adversely affect us, and bankruptcy laws limit our remedies in the event of a tenant default.
Any future public health crisis, pandemic, epidemic or outbreak of infectious disease could have material and adverse effects on our business, operating results, financial condition and cash flows.
Risks Related to Our Organization and Structure
Certain provisions of our governing documents and Maryland law may delay or prevent a transaction or a change of control that might be in the best interest of stockholders.
Our board of directors can take many actions without stockholder approval.
Our rights and the rights of our stockholders to take action against our directors and officers are limited.
Our fiduciary duties as sole member of the general partner of our Operating Partnership could create conflicts of interest, which may impede business decisions that could benefit our stockholders.
Risks Related to Ownership of Our Common Stock
The market price and trading volume of our common stock may be volatile.
The cash available for distribution to stockholders may not be sufficient to make distributions at expected levels, nor can we assure you of our ability to make distributions in the future.

The number of shares of our common stock available for future sale, and future offerings of debt or equity securities may be dilutive to existing stockholders and adversely affect the market price of our common stock.
We have in the past entered, and may in the future enter, into forward sale transactions that subject us to certain risks.
General Real Estate Risks
Our performance is subject to general economic conditions and risks associated with our real estate assets.
We are subject to risks associated with development of real estate.
Real estate investments are not as liquid as other types of investments.
Uninsured losses may adversely affect your returns.
Environmentally hazardous conditions may adversely affect our operating results.
We are exposed to the potential impacts of future climate change and climate change-related risks.
Compliance or failure to comply with the ADA and other regulations could result in substantial costs.
The ownership of properties subject to ground leases exposes us to certain risks.
We may be unable to sell properties, including as a result of uncertain market conditions.
Joint venture investments could be adversely affected by our lack of sole decision-making authority, our reliance on co-venturers' financial condition and disputes between us and our co-venturers.
Risks Related to Our Debt Financings
Our operating results and financial condition could be adversely affected if we are unable to make payments on our debt.
Increases in interest rates could increase our required debt payments and adversely affect our ability to make distributions to stockholders.
Our loan covenants could limit our flexibility and adversely affect our financial condition and ability to make distributions.
If debt is unavailable at reasonable rates, we may not be able to finance acquisitions or refinance our existing debt.
Our hedging strategies may not be successful in mitigating our risks associated with interest rates.
Adverse changes in our credit ratings could negatively affect our financing activity.
paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this report should be carefully considered. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only risks we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we may currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations.

Our operating results and financial condition may be affected by market and economic challenges and uncertainties, which may result from a general economic downturn experienced by the nation as a whole, by the local economies where our properties are located or our tenants conduct business, or by the real estate industry, including the following: (i) poor economic conditions may result in tenant defaults under leases and extended vacancies at our properties; (ii) re-leasing may require concessions or reduced rental rates under the new leases due to reduced demand; (iii) adverse capital and credit market conditions may restrict our operating activities; and (iv) constricted access to credit may result in tenant defaults, non-renewals under leases or inability of potential buyers to acquire properties held for sale.

Also, to the extent we purchase real estate in an unstable market, we are subject to the risk that if the real estate market ceases to attract the same level of capital investment in the future, or the number of companies seeking to acquire properties decreases, the value of our investments may not appreciate or may decrease significantly below the amount we paid for these investments. Our operating results and financial condition could be negatively affected to the extent that an economic slowdown or downturn is prolonged or becomes more severe.

Inflation adversely affects our financing costs (either through near-term borrowings on our variable rate debt, including our unsecured credit facility, or refinancing of existing debt at higher interest rates), and our general and administrative expenses and property operating expenses, as these costs and expenses could increase at a rate higher than our revenue. To the extent our exposure to interest rates is not eliminated through interest rate swaps or other agreements, such increases may also result in higher debt service costs, which will adversely affect our cash flows. Historically, during periods of increasing interest rates, real estate valuations have generally decreased due to rising capitalization rates, which tend to move directionally with interest rates. Consequently, prolonged periods of higher interest rates may negatively impact the valuation of our properties, the market price of our common stock, our ability to raise equity capital on favorable terms, and our future business plans and growth. In addition, our access to funding sources and other credit arrangements could be significantly impaired by factors that affect us, the financial services industry or economy in general, including, among others, liquidity constraints or failures, the ability to perform obligations under financial, credit or liquidity agreements or arrangements, disruptions or instability in the financial services industry or financial markets, or concerns or negative expectations about the prospects for the financial services industry.

The U.S. government indicated its intent to alter its approach to international trade policy and in some cases to renegotiate, or potentially terminate, certain existing trade agreements and treaties with foreign countries, and has made proposals and taken actions related thereto. During 2025, new tariffs were imposed in the United States for imports from a broad range of countries and on certain materials. Several countries also implemented or proposed retaliatory tariffs on imports from the United States and introduced additional trade barriers. Further governmental actions related to the imposition of tariffs or other trade barriers by the United States or foreign countries or changes to international trade agreements or policies, or uncertainty related to any such actions, could further increase costs, decrease margins, reduce the competitiveness of products and services offered by our current and future tenants and adversely affect the revenues and profitability of our tenants whose businesses rely on goods imported from such impacted jurisdictions. Such action, changes or uncertainty could also increase the costs and decrease margins on our development or expansion projects. Any of these impacts could have a material adverse effect on the businesses of our current and future tenants as well as on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

As of December 31, 2025, all our buildings were industrial properties. This concentration exposes us to the risk of economic downturns in the industrial real estate sector to a greater extent than if our properties were diversified across other sectors of the real estate industry.

paragraphs: The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this report. For the definitions of certain terms used in the following discussion, refer to Item 1, "Business - Certain Definitions" included elsewhere in this report.

We are a REIT focused on the acquisition, ownership, and operation of industrial properties throughout the United States. Our platform is designed to (i) identify properties for acquisition that offer relative value across CBRE-EA Tier 1 industrial property types and tenants through the principled application of our proprietary risk assessment model, (ii) provide growth through

sophisticated industrial operation and an attractive opportunity set, and (iii) capitalize our business appropriately given the characteristics of our assets. We are a Maryland corporation and our common stock is publicly traded on the NYSE under the symbol "STAG."

We are organized and conduct our operations to maintain our qualification as a REIT under Sections 856 through 860 of the Code, and generally are not subject to federal income tax to the extent we currently distribute our income to our stockholders and maintain our qualification as a REIT. We remain subject to state and local taxes on our income and property and to U.S. federal income and excise taxes on our undistributed income.

Our qualification and taxation as a REIT depend upon our ability to meet on a continuing basis, through actual annual operating results, qualification tests in the federal income tax laws. Those tests involve the percentage of income that we earn from specified sources, the percentage of our assets that falls within specified categories, the diversity of our capital stock ownership and the percentage of our earnings that we distribute.

As of December 31, 2025, we owned 601 buildings in 41 states with approximately 120.0 million rentable square feet. We own both single- and multi-tenant properties, although the majority of our portfolio is single-tenant.

As of December 31, 2025, our buildings were approximately 96.4% leased, with no single tenant accounting for more than approximately 2.8% of our total annualized base rental revenue and no single industry accounting for more than approximately 11.4% of our total annualized base rental revenue.

We own all of our properties and conduct substantially all of our business through our Operating Partnership, which we control and manage. As of December 31, 2025, we owned approximately 98.1% of the common units in our Operating Partnership, and our current and former executive officers, directors, senior employees and their affiliates, and other third parties owned the remaining 1.9%.

Our ability to increase revenues or cash flow will depend in part on our (i) external growth, specifically acquisition activity, and (ii) internal growth, specifically occupancy and rental rates on our portfolio. A variety of other factors, including those noted below, also affect our future results of operations.

The industrial real estate business is affected by general macro-economic trends including recent changes in interest rates, inflation, trade policies, fiscal policy, technology (e.g., artificial intelligence), and geopolitical tensions. These factors are key drivers of financial market and economic volatility. In 2025, U.S. real gross domestic product ("GDP") declined 0.5% in the first quarter before increasing 3.8% and 4.3% in the subsequent two quarters, respectively. Labor conditions are slowing, with unemployment rising to 4.4% as of December 2025 compared to 4.1% at the end of June 2025. In the fourth quarter of 2025, following weaker employment data, the Federal Open Market Committee lowered the federal funds rate range twice, in each instance a reduction of 25 basis points, to a target range of 3.50-3.75%. Currently, the general consensus among economists is a higher risk of recession or stagflation. While trade policies and macro-economic conditions continue to evolve and could result in tighter credit conditions, weakening tenant cash flows, and rising vacancy rates, we believe we will continue to benefit from having a well-diversified portfolio across various markets, tenant industries, and lease terms. Additionally, we believe that recent moves toward more regional supply chains and geopolitical tensions have accelerated a number of trends that positively impact U.S. industrial demand. However, given the current uncertainty and events discussed above, our acquisition activity has continued to slow since 2022 relative to our historical acquisition pace.

Alternatively, demographic/consumer trends, geopolitical uncertainty and recent legislation supporting U.S. infrastructure may accelerate trends that support stronger long term demand for industrial space, including:

•the continued growth of e-commerce (as compared to the traditional retail store distribution model) and the concomitant demand by e-commerce industry participants for well-located, functional distribution space;

•the increasing attractiveness of the United States as a manufacturing and distribution location because of the size of the U.S. consumer market, an increase in overseas labor costs, policies that promote domestic and regional manufacturing "onshoring and nearshoring," a desire for greater supply chain resilience and redundancy which is driving higher inventory to sales ratios and greater domestic warehouse demand over the long term (i.e. the shortening and fattening of the supply chain); and
•the general quality of the transportation infrastructure in the United States.

paragraphs: "現金租金變動" 係指在該期間內簽訂之租賃契約之基本租金與包含於營運資產組中之可比租賃契約之基本租金的百分比變動。計算方式為比較租賃契約開始後首次應支付的基本租金與租賃契約終止前最後一個月應支付的基本租金，並排除延長租賃期間的租金。對於採用總額租賃或類似類型租賃的租金，會根據適用的可收回費用估計值轉換為淨租金。
"可比租賃" 係指與先前現有租賃契約相比，在相同空間內具有相似租賃結構的租賃契約，不包括我們所有權下未被佔用空間的新租賃契約。
"GAAP" 係指美國通用會計準則。
"新租賃" 係指為任何空置空間簽訂的租賃契約，其初始租賃期限為12個月或更長，包括由新租客或現有租客簽訂的租賃契約，後者為擴展至新（額外）空間。
"佔用率" 係指在財務報表期間結算時，根據GAAP已開始收入確認或租賃期限已開始的總可出租面積百分比，以較早發生者為準。
"營運資產組" 係指已取得並穩定運作或已達成穩定狀態的建築物。營運資產組不包括非核心的靈活/辦公室建築物、包含於價值增加資產組中的建築物，以及被歸類為待售的建築物。
"續約租賃" 係指現有租客簽訂的租賃契約，用以延長租賃期限12個月或更長，包括（i）租賃到期時續約相同空間的租賃，（ii）租賃到期時僅續約部分空間的租命，或（iii）早期續約或協議解決，最終延長原租賃期限12個月或更長。
"平均租金變動" 係指在該期間內簽訂之租賃契約的平均每月基本租金與包含於營運資產組中之可比租賃契約的百分比變動。對於採用總額租賃或類似類型租賃的租金，會根據適用的可收回費用估計值轉換為淨租金，且此計算排除任何延長租賃期間租金的影響。

對於正在開發中或重新開發中的不動產，"穩定"（Stabilization）指較早發生的兩個條件之一：達成90%的租賃率或完成後12個月。針對已取得並立即加入Value Add Portfolio的不動產，(i) 若取得時租賃率低於75%，則"穩定"將在達成90%租賃率或取得後12個月較早發生時實現，或(ii) 若取得後兩年內因已知的租戶搬離而租賃率將低於75%，則"穩定"將在已知租戶搬離後達成90%租賃率或已知租戶搬離後12個月較早發生時實現。
"總年化基礎租金收入"（Total annualized base rental revenue）指截至2025年12月31日，適用不動產或不動產羣的每月基礎現金租金（與我們財務報表中根據GAAP計算的租金不同），乘以12。若租戶在2025年12月31日處於免租期，則年化租金根據首個契約月基礎租金金額乘以12計算。
"Value Add Portfolio"（Value Add Portfolio）指符合以下任一條件的不動產：(i) 取得時租賃率低於75%；(ii) 因已知租戶搬離，取得後兩年內租賃率將低於75%；(iii) 因重大物理翻修而停用；或(iv) 正在開發中。
"加權平均租賃期限"（Weighted Average Lease Term）指在不考慮租戶行使續租權、購置權或提前終止權的情況下，以租賃起始日為基準的契約租賃期限（以年為單位），並按平方呎加權計算。與取得資產相關的加權平均租賃期限反映的是取得時的剩餘租賃期限（以年為單位），並按平方呎加權計算。
本公司為一間專注於美國工業不動產之取得、擁有、開發及營運的REIT。我們的平台設計用以(i) 識別在CBRE-EA Tier 1工業不動產市場、產業及租戶中提供有吸引力回報的不動產，(ii) 透過擁有高品質資產、物業管理及在有吸引力的投資機會中進行取得，實現成長，以及(iii) 根據我們資產的特性適當評估我們的業務。
本公司設立並營運以維持符合1986年美國內收入法典（Internal Revenue Code of 1986）第856至860條項所規定的REIT資格，並一般情況下，只要我們目前將收入分派給股東並維持REIT資格，則不會受到美國聯邦所得稅的影響。我們仍需就所得及不動產課徵州及地方稅，並就未分派所得課徵美國聯邦所得稅及特別稅。

我們是一家以美國為主的工業不動產 REIT，專注於工業不動產之取得、持有與營運。我們的平台設計為 (i) 透過我們專屬風險評估模型的原則性應用，識別提供相對價值之工業不動產，該不動產屬於 CBRE-EA 第一層工業不動產類型及租戶， (ii) 透過 sophisticated 工業營運及吸引人的投資機會來實現成長，以及 (iii) 根據我們資產的特性適當評估我們的業務。
我們是一家馬裏蘭州公司，我們的普通股在紐約證券交易所公開交易，代碼為 "STAG"。
我們的組織與營運方式旨在維持我們作為 REIT 之資格，根據美國稅法第 856 至 860 條款，我們一般不會受到聯邦所得稅之影響，只要我們目前將所得分派給股東並維持作為 REIT 之資格。我們仍需就所得及不動產課徵州及地方稅，並就未分派所得課徵美國聯邦所得稅及調節稅。
我們作為 REIT 之資格與稅務狀況，取決於我們持續透過實際年度營運結果，符合聯邦所得稅法中之資格測試。這些測試涉及我們從特定來源所獲取所得的百分比、我們資產中屬於特定類別的百分比、我們資本股票持有之分散性以及我們分派所得的百分比。

We own both single- and multi-tenant properties, although the majority of our portfolio is single-tenant.', 'translated': '截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有41州共601棟建築物，總計約120.0百萬平方英呎可出租空間。本公司擁有單租戶及多租戶類型的不動產，不過本公司資產組閤中絕大多數為單租戶類型。'}
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的不動產出租率約為 96.4%，且無任何單一租戶佔我們總年化基本租金收入的百分比超過約 2.8%，亦無任何單一產業佔我們總年化基本租金收入的百分比超過約 11.4%。
我們擁有所有不動產，並透過我們的營運合夥企業進行幾乎所有業務活動，我們控制並管理該營運合夥企業。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有營運合夥企業約 98.1% 的普通單位，而我們的現任及前任高階主管、董事、高階員工及其關聯企業，以及其他第三方則持有剩餘的 1.9%。
本公司能否提高營業收入或現金流，將部分取決於我們 (i) 外部成長，特別是收購活動，以及 (ii) 內部成長，特別是我們資產組合的佔用率及租賃率。其他多種因素，包括下列所提及的，也會影響我們未來的營運結果。

工業不動產業務受總體經濟趨勢影響，包括近期利率、通貨膨脹、貿易政策、財政政策、科技（例如人工智慧）以及地緣政治緊張等因素。這些因素是財務市場與經濟波動的主要驅動力。2025 年，美國實質國內生產總值（"GDP"）在第一季下降 0.5%，之後分別在第二季和第三季成長 3.8% 和 4.3%。就業情況放緩，失業率在 2025 年 12 月達到 4.4%，較 2025 年 6 月底的 4.1% 上升。在 2025 年第四季，隨着較弱的就業數據，美國聯邦公開市場委員會兩次降低聯邦資金利率區間，每次降低 25 基點，目標區間降至 3.50-3.75%。目前，經濟學家普遍認為有較高風險面臨經濟衰退或停滯通脹。雖然貿易政策與總體經濟條件持續變化，可能導致信貸條件趨緊、租戶現金流減弱以及空置率上升，我們認為我們仍將受益於在不同市場、租戶產業及租約期限方面具有良好分散的資產組合。此外，我們認為近期朝向更區域化供應鏈以及地緣政治緊張的趨勢，已加速了若干對美國工業需求產生正面影響的趨勢。然而，考慮到目前的不確定性以及上述討論的事件，我們的收購活動自 2022 年以來相較於歷史收購速度已持續減緩。
另一方面，人口/消費者趨勢、地緣政治不確定性以及近期支持美國基礎建設的立法，可能加速支持工業空間長期需求強勁的趨勢，包括：
•電商持續成長（相較於傳統零售商店的分銷模式）以及電商產業參與者對位於優勢地點且功能完善的分銷空間的需求；
•美國作為製造與分銷地點的吸引力增加，這是因為美國消費市場規模、海外勞動成本上升、促進國內及區域製造 "迴流與近岸" 的政策，以及對供應鏈韌性與備援的渴望，這正在驅動長期（即供應鏈縮短與加厚）更高的庫存對銷售比率以及更高的國內倉庫需求；以及
•美國交通基礎建設的整體品質。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
不利之經濟情勢可能對本公司營運成果及財務狀況造成負面影響。
通貨膨脹、利率上升以及影響金融服務業之發展，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及其他營運成果造成負面影響。
貿易政策、關稅及相關政府措施可能導致經濟活動減少，並對本公司業務產生重大負面影響。
本公司之投資集中於工業不動產領域，若該領域發生經濟衰退，將對本公司造成負面影響。
本公司業務受地理及產業集中影響，使其對特定市場及產業之不利事件較為敏感。
本公司許多不動產之擁有時間較短，可能對其特性或缺失缺乏充分了解。
本公司之成長部分取決於取得不動產之併購，可能無法在有利條件下完成併購，且併購後之表現可能未達預期。
我們可能面臨在不熟悉的市場取得不動產相關風險。
我們不動產中相當大一部分的租賃合約將在未來兩年內到期，我們可能無法續約、出租空置空間或以有利條件重新出租空間。
我們面臨租戶方面的激烈競爭，這可能會對我們不動產的佔用率及租金率產生負面影響。
若我們租戶中之一或數家違約，可能會對我們造成重大且不利的影響，且破產法限制我們在租戶違約時的救濟措施。
任何未來的公共衛生危機、疫情、流行病或傳染病爆發都可能對我們的業務、營運成果、財務狀況及現金流產生重大且不利的影響。
與我們組織及結構相關的風險
我們治理文件及馬裏蘭州法律的某些條款可能延遲或阻止一項交易或控制權變更，即使這對股東而言可能為最佳利益。
我們董事會可在無股東批准的情況下採取許多行動。
本公司及股東對董事及高階管理人員採取行動之權利受到限制。
本公司作為經營合夥企業一般合夥人唯一成員的信託義務，可能會產生利益衝突，這可能會阻礙對股東有利的商業決策。
持有本公司普通股的風險
本公司普通股的市場價格及交易量可能波動。
可供分配予股東的現金可能不足以維持預期的分紅水準，本公司亦無法保證未來能否持續進行分紅。
未來可供出售的本公司普通股數量，以及未來發行債務或權益證券的數量，可能對現有股東造成稀釋，並對本公司普通股的市場價格產生負面影響。
本公司過去曾進行，且未來可能進行遠期銷售交易，此等交易可能使本公司面臨某些風險。
一般不動產相關風險
本公司之營運表現受總體經濟環境及不動產資產相關風險影響
本公司受不動產開發相關風險影響
不動產投資之流動性不如其他類型投資
未投保之損失可能對投資人之回報造成不利影響
環境危害條件可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響
本公司面臨未來氣候變遷及相關氣候變遷風險之潛在影響
遵守或未遵守 ADA 及其他法規可能導致重大成本
持有受基地租賃條款約束之不動產可能使本公司面臨某些風險
我們可能無法出售不動產，包括因市場條件不確定所致。
合資企業投資可能因我們缺乏單獨決策權、依賴合資夥伴財務狀況及我們與合資夥伴之間的爭議而受到不利影響。
與我們債務融資相關的風險
若我們無法支付債務本息，將可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
利率上升可能增加我們的債務本息支付需求，並對我們支付股東分紅的能力造成不利影響。
我們的貸款契約可能限制我們的靈活性，並對我們的財務狀況及支付股東分紅的能力造成不利影響。
若無法以合理利率取得債務，我們可能無法籌措資金進行收購或重新融資現有債務。
我們的避險策略可能無法成功降低與利率相關的風險。
本公司信用評級不利變動可能對本公司融資活動產生負面影響。
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本報告中，應謹慎考量。上述風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務運作。

我們的營運成果與財務狀況可能受市場與經濟挑戰與不確定性影響，這些影響可能來自國家整體經歷的經濟衰退、我們資產所在地或租戶營運之地方經濟，或來自不動產業，包括以下內容：(i) 經濟條件不佳可能導致租戶違約或我們資產之空置期延長；(ii) 再出租可能需要讓利或降低租金，因需求減少；(iii) 不利之資本與信貸市場條件可能限制我們之營運活動；以及 (iv) 信貸取得困難可能導致租戶違約、租約到期不續約或潛在買方無法取得待售資產。
此外，若我們在不穩定市場購入不動產，我們將面臨風險，若未來不動產市場無法吸引相同程度之資本投資，或尋求購入資產之公司數量減少，則我們之投資價值可能無法增值，或大幅低於我們購入這些資產之金額。我們之營運成果與財務狀況可能因經濟放緩或衰退延長或變得更嚴重而受到負面影響。

通貨膨脹不利於我們之融資成本（無論是透過短期內變動利率債務之借款，包括我們之無擔保信用融資，或重新融資現有債務時利率提高），以及我們之總體營運與行政費用與不動產營運費用，因這些成本與費用可能以高於我們收入之速率增加。若我們之利率風險未透過利率交換或其他協議消除，這些增加可能導致債務服務成本提高，進而不利於我們之現金流。歷史上，在利率上升期間，不動產評價通常因資本化率上升而下降，而資本化率通常與利率同方向變動。因此，持續高利率期間可能對我們之不動產評價、我們普通股之市場價格、我們以有利條件籌集權益資本之能力，以及我們未來之業務計畫與成長造成負面影響。此外，影響我們、金融服務業或整體經濟之因素，可能顯著影響我們之資金來源與其他信貸安排，包括，但不限於流動性限制或失敗、無法履行金融、信貸或流動性協議或安排之義務、金融服務業或金融市場之幹擾或不穩定，或對金融服務業前景之擔憂或負面預期。

美國政府表示有意改變其國際貿易政策之做法，並在某些情況下重新協商，或可能終止與外國國家之現有貿易協議與條約，並已提出相關建議與採取行動。2025 年，美國對來自廣泛國家之進口商品與特定材料課徵新關稅。若干國家也已實施或提出對來自美國之進口商品之報復性關稅，並引入額外貿易障礙。美國或外國國家進一步針對課徵關稅或其他貿易障礙、國際貿易協議或政策之變更，或與任何此類行動相關之不確定性，可能進一步提高成本、降低邊際率、降低我們現有與未來租戶所提供之產品與服務之競爭力，並對依賴從受影響管轄區進口商品之租戶之收入與利潤造成負面影響。此類行動、變更或不確定性也可能提高我們開發或擴張專案之成本，並降低邊際率。任何這些影響都可能對我們現有與未來租戶之業務，以及我們之業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大負面影響。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們所有大樓均為工業不動產。此集中度使我們面臨工業不動產產業經濟衰退之風險，程度可能高於我們之不動產分散於其他不動產產業部門之情況。
